  {"cp": "CP29", "reasoning": "Section 4-7B(a) requires traceability from the property of origin to receival. Evidence E6 shows receival dockets link grower → farm block → variety → quantity → silo, and E1 describes receival at the intake pit, demonstrating traceability from property to establishment.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Receival dockets link grower → farm block → variety → quantity → silo (E6)"},
  {"cp": "CP30", "reasoning": "Section 4-7B(b) requires traceability while product is at the establishment. Evidence E1 details internal flow: intake pit → conveyor → silo complex/receival shed → auger → outloading hopper. E3 shows Receival → ID Labelling → Segregated Storage → Sampling → Load-out → Dispatch, and E6 assigns unique silo IDs for tracking.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch (E1)"},
  {"cp": "CP31", "reasoning": "Section 4-7B(c) requires traceability to the next premises. Evidence E3 documents seal issue/register check at dispatch and seal verification on arrival. E6 states dispatch bill of lading links silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination, confirming traceability to next premises.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Dispatch: bill of lading links silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination (E6)"},
  {"cp": "CP32", "reasoning": "Sections 4-3(3), 4-7B, 4-8 require a system of controls ensuring traceability and integrity. Evidence E3 explicitly notes deficiencies: lot relabelling reconciled at day-end not point-of-movement, temporary mesh segregation at interim staging bay, and flow chart omitting an alternate transfer path. These gaps undermine the system's ability to ensure compliance.", "verdict": "0", "confidence": 0.85, "cited_evidence": "Some lot relabelling events are reconciled at day-end rather than point-of-movement. One interim staging bay uses temporary mesh segregation pending permanent barrier installation. Flow chart omits one alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods (E3)"},
  {"cp": "CP33", "reasoning": "Sections 4-3(3), 4-7B, 4-8 require a product flow chart demonstrating movement and integrity maintenance. Evidence E3's flow chart omits an alternate transfer path used during peak periods, and E5 explicitly states '[DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan.' The flow chart is incomplete and not standalone as required.", "verdict": "0", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Flow chart omits one alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods (E3) and [DEFICIENCY] No standalone product flow chart diagram attached to this HACCP plan (E5)"},
  {"cp": "CP34", "reasoning": "Sections 4-9 and 9-11 require a system to manage failed goods including blending prohibitions for pest/animal carcase failures and treatment protocols for reassessment. Evidence E5's Failed Goods Procedure addresses GM contamination, mycotoxin, and pesticide MRL exceedances with segregation, hold, re-test, and disposal, but does not address blending restrictions per 4-9(3) or treatment methods per 9-11(2) for prescribed grain failures.", "verdict": "0", "confidence": 0.85, "cited_evidence": "Failed Goods Procedure (AOW-FGP-001): • GM contamination above threshold: lot re-classified as non-Identity Preserved; customer notified; DAFF notified. • Mycotoxin exceedance: silo placed on HOLD; re-test from secondary sample; if confirmed, dispose to non-food use. • Pesticide MRL: reject export consignment; segregate; grower liability documented; option to process to domestic oil (if MRL met under FSANZ) (E5)"},
  {"cp": "CP35", "reasoning": "Sections 4-7A and 4-3(3) require phytosanitary security controls to prevent contamination/infestation. Evidence E3 acknowledges deficiencies: temporary mesh segregation at an interim staging bay pending permanent barrier installation, and flow chart omitting an alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods. These gaps create contamination/infestation risks despite other hygiene and pest controls shown in E2, E6, E8, E11.", "verdict": "0", "confidence": 0.85, "cited_evidence": "One interim staging bay uses temporary mesh segregation pending permanent barrier installation. Flow chart omits one alternate transfer path used during peak receival periods (E3)"},
  {"cp": "CP36", "reasoning": "Section 4-8 requires integrity ensured to minimise substitution risk. Evidence shows layered controls: E3 two-person verification of lot identity and seal recording at dispatch with seal verification on arrival; E6 unique silo IDs and bill of lading linking silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination; E1 segregation via dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones; E5 export-cleared grain in dedicated silos inaccessible to uncleared grain, IP lots in dedicated labelled silos. Despite day-end reconciliation gap, controls minimise substitution risk.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.8, "cited_evidence": "Dispatch controls include two-person verification of lot identity and seal recording. Seal issue/register check at dispatch and seal verification on arrival (E3)"},
  {"cp": "CP37", "reasoning": "Section 4-11 requires packaging meet cleanliness, appropriateness, strength, and importing country requirements where applicable. Evidence E3 notes 'Occasional packaging QC records are attached to shift summary instead of individual lot files,' indicating inadequate record-keeping for packaging quality control. No evidence demonstrates packaging compliance for horticulture exports (mangoes, berries). The deficiency shows the system of controls for packaging is lacking.", "verdict": "0", "confidence": 0.8, "cited_evidence": "Occasional packaging QC records are attached to shift summary instead of individual lot files (E3)"},
  {"cp": "CP38", "reasoning": "Section 11-7 requires retention of traceability records for at least 2 years. Evidence E7 states records retained minimum two years from export activity date, E10 confirms records retained at site for minimum two years from completion, and E13 archive register shows receival/movement/dispatch, treatment, and rejected goods records from Jan 2025 with retention target '>= 2 years.' Legacy index migration does not negate retention compliance.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity (E7) and Receival/Movement/Dispatch | Jan 2025 - current | Secure digital archive | >= 2 years | Legacy index migration in progress (E13)"},
  {"cp": "CP39", "reasoning": "Section 11-7 requires retention of rejected/failed goods records for at least 2 years. Evidence E5 states all non-conformances recorded in AOW-NCR register with root cause analysis, and E13 archive register shows 'Rejected/failed goods | Jan 2025 - current | Compliance archive | >= 2 years | Rejected-goods archive verified,' demonstrating compliant retention.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Rejected/failed goods | Jan 2025 - current | Compliance archive | >= 2 years | Rejected-goods archive verified (E13)"},
  {"cp": "CP40", "reasoning": "Section 11-2 requires records in English, dated, accurate, legible, auditable. Evidence E10 shows cleaning log template with Date field and English entries, E13 digital archive ensures legibility and auditability. No evidence of non-English, undated, or illegible records for this establishment; E14's issues pertain to a different establishment.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.9, "cited_evidence": "Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system... Date | Area / Equipment | Cleaning Method | Chemical Used | Operator Name | Verified By | Comments (E10)"},
  {"cp": "CP41", "reasoning": "Section 4-7 requires all importing country requirements be met. Evidence E1 documents Japan's requirements (Phytosanitary Certificate, residue compliance with Positive List System, MAFF pre-clearance). E7 notes mycotoxin limits for wheat. The HACCP plan (E5, E9) includes CCPs for pesticide MRL (CCP-1) and mycotoxins (CCP-2), and phytosanitary procedure (E3) includes DAFF sampling before loading, showing systems to meet documented requirements.", "verdict": "1", "confidence": 0.85, "cited_evidence": "Requirement | Details Phytosanitary Certificate | PC required; declare freedom from stripe rust, Tilletia spp. and listed nematodes Residue Compliance | Pesticide residues must comply with Japan's Positive List System Pre-clearance | MAFF pre-clearance inspection may be required for high-risk consignments (E1)"}
